item.title: When Everything Is a Heat Wave and Every Change Is Climate
item.description: In the end, the paper offers a compelling story, but not a disciplined causal argument. A loosely defined marine heat wave is paired with a loosely defined ecological baseline, and the two are joined by temporal coincidence and confident language. The synthesis feels objective because it is large and comprehensive, not because its foundations are secure.

item.title: They called me the “anti-Greta” so I was targeted
item.description: Why do they fear me? I’m young, have a fresh voice, and am skilled at charts and data analysis. Turns out, I’m also pretty good at using humor to re-examine the facts that are not kind to those who view climate as their path to power.

item.title: Climate Policies Make California Unaffordable, LAist, Not Climate Change
item.description: LAist is simply pursuing a climate alarmist angle in this story, while downplaying the larger and frankly blatant influences on the state’s cost of living crisis. California is known for having some of the best climate regions in the world, the easiest to live in, and that has not changed. What has changed is the population, and the insidious growth of climate policies by state leadership, prioritized over public welfare.

item.title: Think tank IREF: ‘Against All Rationality, the EU Persists in its Net-Zero Delusion’
item.description: Simple arithmetic already raises red flags. EU emissions fell by 37% over the 33 years from 1990 to today. Achieving an additional 68% reduction in just 17 years would require nearly tripling the pace of decarbonization.
